text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's Austrian newspapers:
- Experts are more optimstic about Austria's economy based on a pick-up in exports and investments.
- Finance Minister Viktor Klima plans to wait on further reports on the bids for Creditanstalt before naming the future owner of the bank before the end of the year.
- Retailers Meinl and Loewa plan to cooperate in logistics in a bid to stand up to the expanding Billa and Spar chains.
- Austrian Airlines has placed an order for four new Airbus planes worth four billion schillings.
- The federal chamber of Austria's parliament has recommended the government not to sell Creditanstalt to Bank Austria before the latter has itself been privatised.
- OECD expects a rise in Austrian unemployment in the next year, but sees it coming down again in 1998.
- Raiffesien Zentralbank has renewed its interest in taking over a major stake in postal saving's bank PSK, but says it would prefer PSK not to be able to sell private loans.
- OECD says austerity moves by the government will not be enough to reach the Maastricht criteria for Europe's single currency.
- Even though Austrians want European integration to speed up, a majority is against the introduction of the single European currency, a survey shows.
- Amid worsening relations in Austria's coalition government, the sale of Creditanstalt has now been delegated to the party chiefs.

- Raiffeisen Zentralbank's (RZB) operating profit is expected to have risen 14 percent to 1.7 billion schillings in 1996. RZB is interested in taking over 49 percent of postal saving's bank PSK, while the rest should be kept by the postal investment holding.
- The debts of Austria's provinces are too high if Austria wants to meet the European Union's Maastricht criteria.
- The battle within the coalition government over how to privatise Creditanstalt is bringing conservative junior coalition partners People's Party and the far-right Freedom Party closer together.
- The political rows accompanying the privatisation of Creditanstalt have lead to turbulent share price moves in the bank's stocks.
